# Education in Greece – Key Overview
Education in Greece is structured into three main stages: primary, secondary (comprising lower and upper levels), and tertiary (higher education). Preschool is compulsory and lasts two years—one year of pre-kindergarten and one year of kindergarten—followed by six years of primary school (Dimotiko), which is also compulsory. Primary education emphasizes core subjects and foreign language acquisition, with English introduced from kindergarten. Lower secondary education consists of three years at Gymnasium, which is mandatory, with a national curriculum and automatic enrollment from primary school. Upper secondary education includes Lyceum (general or vocational), lasting three years, with options such as General Lyceum (academic focus), Vocational Lyceum (EPAL, which provides dual diplomas and specialization in several fields), and specialized schools (music, arts, ecclesiastical, etc.). Students must pass standardized Pan-Hellenic Examinations to access higher education.
Higher education is provided by public and (as of 2024) accredited private institutions (HEIs), including universities and academies. Admission is determined by academic performance and exam results. Public HEIs are tuition-free for undergraduate studies, with free textbooks and meal provisions for many students. Post-secondary vocational options include Schools of Advanced Vocational Training (SAEK) and various apprenticeships; professional diplomas are awarded according to the Hellenic Qualification Framework (HQF), which is aligned to European standards. Lifelong learning and non-formal education providers, such as open courses and digital academies, offer additional training opportunities outside the formal system. The education system is managed by the Ministry of Education, with a history of reforms, special education initiatives, and a range of programmatic choices in both academic and vocational pathways.
